scenarios.promptText: You didn't get the job you really wanted.

responses.option: I guess I'm just not good enough.
responses.feedback: This reinforces a limiting belief and closes the door to growth. It's disempowering and likely untrue.

responses.option: The hiring process is random sometimes—who knows what they were looking for.
responses.feedback: This is a neutral take that avoids spiraling but also avoids growth. Accepting, but passive.

responses.option: This wasn't the right fit, but something better is lining up. I've gained clarity through the process.
responses.feedback: Empowering interpretation. You're taking agency and trusting in alignment. Strong mindset.

responses.option: They probably just wanted someone who would play the corporate game.
responses.feedback: This seems confident, but it's blame masked as empowerment. It may keep you feeling superior but stuck.

scenarios.promptText: You texted someone something meaningful and they ghosted.

responses.option: I shouldn't have been so vulnerable. I always mess this stuff up.
responses.feedback: This is a disempowering conclusion rooted in shame. It's not necessarily true and reinforces unworthiness.

responses.option: Maybe they just didn't know how to respond. Ghosting says more about them than me.
responses.feedback: A neutral interpretation that avoids self-blame. It creates emotional distance from the event.

responses.option: That message came from a real place, and I stand by it. I want someone who values that kind of honesty.
responses.feedback: Strong and empowering. You're affirming your values and openness, not letting the response define you.

responses.option: Some people ghost when you're actually real with them. They prob weren't worth my time anyway.
responses.feedback: Feels strong but slightly defensive. It may be a self-protective story that avoids feeling the hurt.

scenarios.promptText: You had a disagreement with a close friend and haven't talked in days.

responses.option: I must have done something wrong. I always mess up relationships.
responses.feedback: This reflects self-blame and could reinforce feelings of inadequacy. It's important to acknowledge both sides in disagreements.

responses.option: Maybe they just need space. I don't need to take it personally.
responses.feedback: A healthy approach that offers perspective, allowing room for understanding without internalizing the issue.

responses.option: It's frustrating, but I know we'll work it out eventually. Every relationship has its ups and downs.
responses.feedback: This is an empowering and realistic approach, understanding that conflict is natural and temporary.

responses.option: If they can't communicate properly, maybe I don't need them in my life.
responses.feedback: This may come from a place of defensiveness, closing off emotional connection instead of fostering open dialogue.

scenarios.promptText: You received a critical comment online about something you created.

responses.option: This person is just a hater. They don't know what they're talking about.
responses.feedback: This response is defensive and dismissive, potentially blocking growth. It's important to consider valid feedback, even from critics.

responses.option: Not everyone will like what I do. It's just one opinion out of many.
responses.feedback: A balanced perspective, recognizing that different opinions are natural and don't define your worth or work.

responses.option: I'll use this criticism to improve and make my work even better next time.
responses.feedback: A positive and constructive mindset. This approach shows resilience and a commitment to learning and growing from feedback.

responses.option: They clearly don't appreciate the effort that went into it. I should stop sharing my work online.
responses.feedback: This response might stem from discouragement. It's important to keep sharing and growing, even in the face of criticism.

scenarios.promptText: You made a mistake at work that impacted the project you were working on.

responses.option: I should have known better. This is going to ruin everything.
responses.feedback: This thought focuses on shame and self-criticism. Mistakes happen, and they don't define your overall performance.

responses.option: It's an unfortunate mistake, but I'll fix it and learn from it. Everyone makes mistakes.
responses.feedback: A realistic and empowering approach. Acknowledging the mistake and focusing on the solution shows resilience and growth.

responses.option: I feel like I'm always messing things up. Maybe I'm not cut out for this job.
responses.feedback: This thought leans toward self-doubt and should be re-framed. Mistakes are part of any job, and they don't define your abilities.

responses.option: I can use this as a chance to show how well I can recover and learn from this situation.
responses.feedback: This is an empowering mindset that shows growth, adaptability, and a focus on improvement, rather than getting stuck in the mistake.

scenarios.promptText: You were invited to an event but didn't feel like you fit in with the crowd.

responses.option: I'm just not social enough. I always feel awkward in these situations.
responses.feedback: This reinforces a limiting belief. Feeling awkward is normal, and it doesn't define your social abilities or worth.

responses.option: It's okay. Not every event is for everyone. I'll just enjoy myself in my own way.
responses.feedback: A healthy and empowering approach that acknowledges personal preferences and removes pressure to conform.

responses.option: I didn't vibe with anyone, but I can use this experience to work on my social skills next time.
responses.feedback: A constructive take that focuses on growth and improving social experiences without judgment or shame.

responses.option: I just don't belong in this circle. Maybe I shouldn't go to events like this anymore.
responses.feedback: This response is quite dismissive and final. It may be worth exploring the discomfort rather than isolating yourself from future events.

scenarios.promptText: You received feedback from your boss that your performance needs improvement.

responses.option: I'm never good enough for them. I can't seem to do anything right.
responses.feedback: This reflects a negative self-judgment that can lead to a fixed mindset. It's important to view feedback as an opportunity to improve, not as a personal failure.

responses.option: I'll take this feedback and see what I can work on. Everyone has areas to improve.
responses.feedback: A growth mindset response. Acknowledging that feedback is part of development and not an attack on your abilities.

responses.option: I need to put in more effort and prove myself next time. I won't let this define me.
responses.feedback: This is an empowering and motivating approach, focusing on self-improvement and resilience.

responses.option: Maybe this job isn't for me. If I can't get it right, what am I even doing here?
responses.feedback: This response leans toward defeatism and may be a reaction to frustration. It's crucial to reframe setbacks as growth opportunities rather than reasons to give up.

scenarios.promptText: You posted something on social media that you were really proud of, but it didn't get the feedback you were hoping for.

responses.option: Maybe my post wasn't good enough. No one seems to care.
responses.feedback: This response focuses on self-doubt and can lead to feelings of unworthiness. Remember, engagement doesn't always reflect the value of your work.

responses.option: Social media is unpredictable. Sometimes things just don't land the way you expect them to.
responses.feedback: A healthy and realistic perspective. Recognizing that external factors often play a role can prevent unnecessary self-judgment.

responses.option: I know the content I shared is meaningful, and I'll keep posting things that reflect who I am.
responses.feedback: An empowering mindset that focuses on staying true to your values and continuing to create meaningful content, regardless of external validation.

responses.option: Maybe people just don't get it. I'm done trying to impress others online.
responses.feedback: This may be a defense mechanism, detaching from the disappointment. It's important to find a balance between authenticity and staying open to feedback.

scenarios.promptText: You missed an important opportunity that you've been preparing for.

responses.option: I just can't catch a break. Maybe I'm not meant for this.
responses.feedback: This response leans into defeatism. It's important to remember that setbacks are a natural part of growth, not signs of failure.

responses.option: I missed it this time, but there will be more chances. I'll learn from this one.
responses.feedback: This is a growth-oriented perspective. It's an empowering response that acknowledges setbacks but focuses on future opportunities.

responses.option: I should've been more prepared. It's all my fault.
responses.feedback: Self-blame can limit growth. Instead of blaming yourself, focus on what can be improved for the future.

responses.option: I think this opportunity just wasn't meant for me, and that's okay. Something better might come along.
responses.feedback: This response is grounded in acceptance and trust. It's about recognizing that sometimes, things don't align for a reason.

scenarios.promptText: You and a close friend had a misunderstanding, and now there's distance between you two.

responses.option: They should've understood me better. I'm not sure I want to try anymore.
responses.feedback: This response may cause further distance. It's important to communicate openly and give the other person the chance to explain their perspective.

responses.option: Misunderstandings happen, but I'm willing to talk it out and clear the air.
responses.feedback: This approach is solution-focused and healthy. It emphasizes the importance of communication in maintaining relationships.

responses.option: Maybe this friendship isn't worth the effort if this keeps happening.
responses.feedback: This response can indicate frustration, but it's important to reflect on the overall value of the relationship before making hasty decisions.

responses.option: I know we both have our flaws, and it might take time to rebuild trust. I'm open to that process.
responses.feedback: This response is mature and grounded in emotional intelligence. Acknowledging both sides and being open to growth is key to healing.

scenarios.promptText: You've been putting off a big task that you've been dreading, and now the deadline is fast approaching.

responses.option: I always procrastinate. I'm never going to get it done on time.
responses.feedback: This response is self-defeating and focuses on past behaviors. Instead of labeling yourself, focus on taking small, actionable steps toward completion.

responses.option: I've left this too late, but I'll do what I can to make it work. It's not ideal, but I can still try.
responses.feedback: This is a realistic, action-oriented response. Acknowledging the situation while still focusing on effort is empowering.

responses.option: I'm just going to accept that I won't be able to do my best, but at least I'll have something to show.
responses.feedback: While this response shows some acceptance, it may indicate resignation. Aim to give yourself permission to do your best, even under time constraints.

responses.option: I'll take a deep breath, break this down into smaller tasks, and get started now. It's all about progress, not perfection.
responses.feedback: This response is highly proactive and focused on positive momentum. Breaking down the task helps make it feel less overwhelming and more manageable.

scenarios.promptText: You set a big goal and didn't reach it.

responses.option: I guess I wasn't meant for this goal.
responses.feedback: This response shuts down growth and aligns with a fixed mindset. It's important to see failure as part of the learning process.

responses.option: Maybe I wasn't fully committed or focused enough. I'll reassess and try again.
responses.feedback: This response is balanced and shows ownership. You're accepting responsibility while still leaving room for improvement.

responses.option: I learned a lot through the process, and the goal might not be aligned with where I'm headed anyway.
responses.feedback: A growth-oriented response. You're framing the failure as part of the journey and possibly reevaluating your goal.

responses.option: This goal was unrealistic from the start. Time to shift priorities.
responses.feedback: This is a realistic take. Sometimes, reassessing goals based on new information is the best way forward.

scenarios.promptText: You tried to give a speech or presentation, but you felt like it didn't go well.

responses.option: I must have been terrible. Everyone probably thinks I'm not good at this.
responses.feedback: This is a self-critical response. It's important to view any public speaking experience as a learning opportunity rather than a failure.

responses.option: It wasn't perfect, but I got through it. I'll focus on what I can improve next time.
responses.feedback: This is a healthy, growth-focused perspective. You acknowledge the difficulty but embrace learning from it.

responses.option: I was nervous, but I'll try again next time and work on my presentation skills.
responses.feedback: This shows self-compassion and a willingness to improve. You're treating the experience as part of a larger process.

responses.option: I felt uncomfortable, but everyone has moments like this. It's not the end of the world.
responses.feedback: This response shows resilience. You acknowledge the challenge but maintain a healthy perspective on setbacks.

scenarios.promptText: You received a compliment on something you don't feel you deserve praise for.

responses.option: I don't deserve this compliment. They're just being nice.
responses.feedback: This response dismisses the compliment and minimizes your accomplishments. It's important to allow yourself to accept positive feedback.

responses.option: I appreciate the compliment, even if it feels undeserved. Maybe I'm being too hard on myself.
responses.feedback: This response shows openness to receiving positive feedback, and it also acknowledges self-compassion.

responses.option: I've put in the effort, so maybe I do deserve it after all.
responses.feedback: This response reflects growth and acknowledgment of your efforts. It shows you're learning to accept recognition.

responses.option: I'll take the compliment graciously, even if it doesn't feel totally deserved.
responses.feedback: This is a healthy response, showing you're working on embracing positive feedback without overthinking it.

scenarios.promptText: You were excited about a new project but realized it's more challenging than you expected.

responses.option: Maybe I'm not cut out for this. I should have stuck to what I know.
responses.feedback: This response is defeatist. It's important to see challenges as part of growth rather than reasons to give up.

responses.option: It's difficult, but I can learn and adapt. I'll take it one step at a time.
responses.feedback: This is a positive mindset. You're embracing the challenge and choosing to move forward with a learning approach.

responses.option: I'm feeling overwhelmed, but I know I can ask for help and get through it.
responses.feedback: This response reflects self-awareness and a willingness to seek support when needed. It shows maturity in managing challenges.

responses.option: It's harder than I thought, but I'm committed to pushing through and making it work.
responses.feedback: This response shows resilience and determination. You're embracing the challenge and committing to the process.

scenarios.promptText: You made plans with someone, but they canceled at the last minute.

responses.option: I guess they didn't care enough to follow through. I feel let down.
responses.feedback: This is an emotional, negative interpretation. It's important to separate their actions from your self-worth.

responses.option: It's disappointing, but things happen. I'll be open to rescheduling when they're ready.
responses.feedback: This response shows understanding and patience. You're not taking it personally and are keeping the door open for future plans.

responses.option: It's frustrating, but I'll use the extra time for something productive or relaxing.
responses.feedback: This is a healthy way to reframe the situation. You're making the most of the unexpected change in plans.

responses.option: I'm disappointed, but I know they have their reasons. I'll give them space.
responses.feedback: This response shows maturity and empathy. You're allowing for the possibility that their cancellation was out of their control.

scenarios.promptText: You took a risk by sharing an idea with others, but it didn't get the response you hoped for.

responses.option: I should have kept it to myself. I guess my ideas are not good enough.
responses.feedback: This response is overly self-critical. Every idea is an opportunity to learn and improve, regardless of the immediate response.

responses.option: It didn't land as I hoped, but I'll refine it and try again.
responses.feedback: This is a healthy mindset. You're viewing the situation as a learning experience and embracing the possibility of future success.

responses.option: Not everyone will get it, but I believe in the value of my idea and will keep pushing forward.
responses.feedback: This response reflects confidence and persistence. You're recognizing that not everyone will always understand, but that doesn't diminish the value of your ideas.

responses.option: Maybe I'm not ready for this, but I'll take the feedback and work on improving.
responses.feedback: This response shows openness to constructive criticism. You're committed to growth and willing to refine your approach.

scenarios.promptText: You committed to a new habit or routine but found it harder to maintain than you thought.

responses.option: I guess I just don't have the discipline for this. It's too difficult.
responses.feedback: This is a defeatist response. Maintaining new habits takes time and patience. It's important to be kind to yourself in the process.

responses.option: It's harder than I expected, but I'll make adjustments and keep trying.
responses.feedback: This shows resilience. You're acknowledging the challenge while staying focused on your goal and willing to adjust along the way.

responses.option: Maybe I need a different approach or some extra support to make this work.
responses.feedback: This response reflects flexibility and a proactive approach to problem-solving. You're not giving up; you're adjusting your strategy.

responses.option: It's been tough, but I'll keep pushing through and trust the process.
responses.feedback: This is a determined, growth-oriented mindset. You're sticking with it despite the difficulty, which shows perseverance.

scenarios.promptText: You had an argument with a family member, and now there's tension between you two.

responses.option: I feel like things will never be the same again. I've probably ruined our relationship.
responses.feedback: This response is extreme and pessimistic. Conflict doesn't necessarily mean the end of a relationship, but rather an opportunity for growth and understanding.

responses.option: I'm upset, but I'll give it time and space to cool off before trying to talk things through.
responses.feedback: This is a balanced response. You're acknowledging your emotions while also recognizing the need for reflection and calm before attempting resolution.

responses.option: We'll get through this. I'll reach out and try to clear the air when the time is right.
responses.feedback: This shows maturity and a willingness to repair the relationship. You're taking responsibility and planning for a positive resolution.

responses.option: I don't know how to fix things, but I know I can work on how I approach the situation.
responses.feedback: This is a self-aware response. You're focusing on your own approach and emotional regulation, which is a positive step toward resolution.

scenarios.promptText: You tried something new, but it didn't turn out as well as you hoped.

responses.option: I knew I wouldn't be good at it. I should have stuck with what I know.
responses.feedback: This is a self-limiting belief. Trying new things is a learning experience, and success often comes with repeated attempts and adjustments.

responses.option: It didn't work this time, but I learned from it and will try again with a new approach.
responses.feedback: This is a growth mindset. You're seeing the experience as an opportunity to learn and improve, rather than viewing it as a failure.

responses.option: I didn't get the results I wanted, but it was still a valuable experience, and I'm proud I tried.
responses.feedback: This response highlights self-compassion. You're focusing on the courage to try rather than just the outcome.

responses.option: I made mistakes, but I'll keep practicing and refining. Progress takes time.
responses.feedback: This is a healthy, persistent mindset. You're embracing the process of improvement and understanding that mastery requires practice.

scenarios.promptText: You expressed your feelings to someone you're interested in, but they didn't feel the same way.

responses.option: I should've known better. I was probably just imagining things.
responses.feedback: This response focuses on self-blame and regret. It's natural to feel disappointment, but it's important to remember that rejection is a part of life and doesn't reflect your worth.

responses.option: It stings, but I'm proud of myself for being honest about my feelings. I'll be okay.
responses.feedback: This is a healthy and empowering take. Acknowledging the courage it took to express yourself shows strength and emotional maturity.

responses.option: Maybe they were just not the right person for me. I'll keep looking for someone who values me.
responses.feedback: This response demonstrates resilience and a healthy mindset. It acknowledges that the right person is out there, and it's okay for things not to work out with this one.

responses.option: That was embarrassing. I don't think I'll ever put myself out there like that again.
responses.feedback: This response reflects disappointment and fear of vulnerability. While it's normal to feel hurt, it's important to remind yourself that rejection doesn't define your ability to love or be loved.

scenarios.promptText: You've been working hard on a personal project, but it's taking longer to complete than you anticipated.

responses.option: I'm frustrated. It's taking way longer than I thought. Maybe it's not worth it.
responses.feedback: This response reflects frustration and potential discouragement. It's important to be patient with yourself and trust that progress takes time.

responses.option: I underestimated the time it would take, but I'll keep pushing through and make steady progress.
responses.feedback: This is a resilient and proactive mindset. You're acknowledging the challenge while continuing to move forward at a manageable pace.

responses.option: It's taking longer than expected, but I'm learning a lot along the way, and that's valuable.
responses.feedback: This response shows perspective and focus on growth. Even if it takes longer, the process is teaching you important lessons.

responses.option: I'm not where I thought I'd be, but I'm proud of the progress I've made so far.
responses.feedback: This response emphasizes self-compassion and pride in the effort put forth, regardless of the timeline.
